zones.description: Residential towers and stepped perimeter blocks positioned away from the noisiest highway frontage provide compact urban housing with landscaped internal courtyards.
Ground-floor grocery store, cafés, pharmacies, and neighborhood services activate pedestrian streets and ensure daily amenities within walking distance.
Preserved red-brick workshops, factory chimneys, and fragments of railway infrastructure are adaptively reused as galleries, creative studios, and public exhibition spaces.
Flexible office and coworking buildings support employment generation and integrate with the wider multifunctional redevelopment strategy.
A centrally located kindergarten with protected play courtyards and community rooms provides safe access for nearby residential blocks.
Public green corridor with pedestrian and cycling routes follows former railway alignments and links preserved industrial heritage spaces.
Acoustic landscape berms, service roads, and structured parking along Entuziastov Highway reduce traffic noise impacts and improve pedestrian safety.

facts: Maximum building height does not exceed 30 floors.
Green and public open spaces exceed the required minimum of 15% of the territory.
Historic factory chimneys and selected red-brick industrial buildings are preserved and adaptively reused.
Noise mitigation measures are concentrated along Entuziastov Highway through landscaped buffers and building placement.
At least one kindergarten and one grocery store are provided within walking distance of all residential blocks.
Former railway sidings are partially integrated into the landscape design as industrial heritage elements.
The redevelopment creates a mixed-use urban quarter connected to the existing Lefortovo residential district.
Ground floors along main pedestrian routes are dedicated to active commercial and public uses.
